quote_zh: To a clean and pre-dried 100mL round bottomed flask, dichloromethane (10mL) NMSBA (1.0g, 0.004mol) and N, N’-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (DCC) (0.8g, 0.004mol) were added under stirring at the temperature of 25-30°C. Tothismixture, 1, 3-cyclohexanedione (0.45g, 0.004mol) was added and stirred for about 2 hours at 25-30°C. The reaction mixture was quenched with water (10mL) and separated the organic layer. The organic layer obtained was concentrated to obtain enol ester as off white crystalline solid. HPLC purity > 85%; Yield: 0.89g (65%); Melting point 152-158°C.
arithmetic_check: Four printed figures bear on the arithmetic, three mass/mole pairs and a mass with a yield percentage, and ALL OF THEM CLOSE. No arithmetic flag raised, nothing corrected. Molecular weights computed with RDKit from the structures the document draws for these compounds elsewhere. PAIR 1, NMSBA: 1.0 g / 245.212 g/mol (C8H7NO6S, from CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1) = 0.0040781 mol, which at the printed three-decimal precision is 0.004 mol, exactly as printed. PAIR 2, 1,3-cyclohexanedione: 0.45 g / 112.128 g/mol (C6H8O2, from O=C1CCCC(=O)C1) = 0.0040133 mol, printed 0.004 mol. PAIR 3, DCC: 0.8 g / 206.333 g/mol (C13H22N2, from C1CCCCC1N=C=NC1CCCCC1) = 0.0038773 mol, printed 0.004 mol; it rounds to the printed figure, the rounding window of 0.004 mol at this precision (0.0035 to 0.0045 mol) containing it comfortably. So molar_mass_inconsistent is not raised on any of the three, in contrast to Example 1, whose NMST pair implies 220.1 g/mol against a true 215.23. MASS BALANCE: the three charges are printed as equimolar at 0.004 mol, so 0.004 mol is the limiting charge however one reads it, and the product is C14H13NO7S at 339.325 g/mol (from CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)OC2=CC(=O)CCC2)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1). The printed 0.89 g against that limiting charge is 65.6% of theory, against the printed 65%, a difference of six tenths of a percentage point and well inside the rounding of a whole-number yield. Testing the same 0.89 g against the charges as weighed rather than as printed in moles brackets it: on the NMSBA's actual 0.0040781 mol it is 64.3%, and on the dione's actual 0.0040133 mol it is 65.4%. Every one of the three readings lands within about one point of the printed 65%, so the mass, the moles and the yield are mutually consistent and mass_balance_implausible is NOT raised. This confirms independently what the A1 pass found for this section. The theoretical mass these ratios are computed against is a derived quantity that appears NOWHERE in the patent, so it was kept out of reactions.json entirely, out of the record's notes, and out of every numeric field; it exists only in this provenance line, which A5 reads and which never enters the gold record. STOICHIOMETRY, computed but deliberately not written into the record because the patent states no equivalents and molar_ratio_text is therefore null: 1.00 : 0.98 : 0.95 for NMSBA : dione : DCC on the charges as weighed, i.e. nominally equimolar, and 1 : 1 : 1 on the moles as printed. PURITY IS A MEASURED BOUND, NOT A SPECIFICATION: line 310 prints "HPLC purity > 85%" for the single batch this Example made, so product_purity_pct is 85.0 with purity_method hplc, the inequality kept verbatim in quote_zh, in procedure_text and in the record notes, and 85.0 read as that printed lower bound rather than an assayed equality. A1 holds the same 85.0 with raw_text "HPLC purity > 85%" for the same compound. The summary section's "at least 65%" and "at least 85%" are specifications of the invention in general, are not measurements, and entered no field of this record. NOT CHECKABLE: no mass is printed for the dichloromethane or the quench water, both being volumes, so neither admits a molecular-weight check, and neither was flagged. No isolated mass is printed for NMSBA by any of Examples 1 to 3, so this section's 1.0 g charge cannot be compared against an upstream output and scale_discontinuity could not be evaluated; it is recorded as unevaluable, not as passing.
